extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the NDSEG Fellowship (U.S. citizens and nationals; STEM graduate students)
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility rules for applying to the Department of Defense NDSEG (National Defense Science and Engineering Graduate) Fellowship, specifying citizenship, academic status, allowable disciplines, and ability to accept the fellowship benefits and terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall eligibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four eligibility requirements: citizenship, discipline, academic status, and the ability to accept the full benefit. Applicants must meet all four requirements to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must satisfy all four listed categories (no partial waivers indicated). This statement functions as the top-level gate for all applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: The NDSEG Fellowship Program is open only to applicants who are citizens or nationals of the United States. The term "nationals" refers to native residents of a possession of the United States such as American Samoa. It does not refer to a citizen of another country who has applied for U.S. citizenship. Persons who hold permanent resident status are not eligible. Proof of citizenship will be required upon formal offer. Dual Citizens are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key exclusions/inclusions: permanent residents (green card holders) are explicitly ineligible; dual citizens are allowed; U.S. nationals (e.g., American Samoa residents) are eligible; proof of citizenship required at offer stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic status / Education timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are eligible if they have received or will receive a baccalaureate degree in the year of their fellowship application, are within first two years of their graduate study for a traditional program (Graduate (1st-2nd year), or within the first two years of a PhD (1st-2nd year) in science or engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifying example given: if in Fall 2022 you are currently in your second year of a PhD program, you would be entering your third year and remain eligible; if you are entering your fourth year or more in a traditional PhD program you would not be eligible. Interpretation: eligibility is limited to very early-stage graduate students (first or second year) or those finishing baccalaureate the year of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline / Major requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Must major in one of the following disciplines: Aeronautical and Astronautical Engineering; Astrodynamics*; Biomedical Engineering; Biosciences (includes toxicology); Chemical Engineering; Chemistry; Civil Engineering; Cognitive, Neural, and Behavioral Sciences (Note:PsyD programs are not eligible); Computer and Computational Sciences; Electrical Engineering; Geosciences (includes terrain, water, and air); Materials Science and Engineering (including Materials for Extreme Environments); Mathematics; Mechanical Engineering; Naval Architecture and Ocean Engineering (includes undersea systems); Oceanography (includes ocean acoustics, remote sensing, and marine meteorology); Physics (including optics); Space Physics*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The U.S. Space Force additions (e.g., Astrodynamics) are noted; PsyD programs are explicitly ineligible under cognitive/neural/behavioral sciences. The page also states: "Areas of interest that fall outside of the list may be considered if it is a STEM field and is related to one or more of these fields." Applicants unsure which discipline to select are advised to consult their academic or research advisor for guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to accept the fellowship (degree intent, start date, enrollment, and institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Must intend to pursue a doctoral degree in order to be eligible for NDSEG Fellowship support. If awarded, you must start your tenure in the fall of that year. Fellowships awarded in the spring of 2022 must start in September 2022. Deferrals may be considered on a case by case basis, and must be authorized by NDSEG prior to acceptance. In most cases an NDSEG Fellowship is non-deferrable. NDSEG Fellows must be enrolled full-time and must be pursuing graduate study at a U.S. institution; the NDSEG Fellowship does not pay for tuition at any non-U.S. institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must plan to begin/continue toward a PhD starting in the fellowship's fall start term. Deferral is uncommon and requires prior NDSEG authorization. Enrollment must be full-time at a U.S. institution because the program will not fund tuition at institutions outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous remuneration and benefit-acceptance restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellow may not accept simultaneous remuneration from another major fellowship. Fellows must be eligible to accept both the tuition benefit and the full stipend amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who hold or expect to hold other major fellowships that provide stipend/tuition must ensure they can decline or forego simultaneous benefits; NDSEG expects fellows to be able to accept the program's full financial package (tuition benefit plus full stipend).
